markingScheme.criterion: States that the pondweed cell had a rigid, regular (brick-like) cell wall, while the cheek cell had no wall — only a soft, irregular folded outline.
markingScheme.accept: Equivalent wording (e.g. 'straight edges' vs 'wobbly/rounded edges'); exact terms like 'brick-like' are not required if the wall/no-wall contrast is clear.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying the cells 'look different' with no mention of the wall specifically.

markingScheme.criterion: States that the pondweed cell contained visible green chloroplasts — structures never seen in the cheek cell photo.
markingScheme.accept: Any correct reference to chloroplasts (or 'green structures') being present only in the plant cell photo.
markingScheme.insufficient: Mentioning 'green colour' without identifying it as chloroplasts, or omitting this feature entirely.

markingScheme.criterion: Recognises that both cells also showed shared structures (e.g. cytoplasm, and a nucleus-like region in the cheek cell), and explicitly states it was the presence of the wall and chloroplasts — not the shared features — that identified the plant cell.
markingScheme.accept: Any correct naming of at least one shared structure, paired with the point that shared structures cannot be used to distinguish the two cell types.
markingScheme.insufficient: Naming a shared structure without explaining that it does NOT help tell the cells apart.

markingScheme.criterion: Correctly identifies it as a plant cell, stating that animal cells never have a cell wall or chloroplasts under any circumstances, so finding even one of these features is enough to rule out an animal cell.
markingScheme.accept: Any correct identification with a reason naming the wall and/or chloroplasts as the diagnostic feature.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying 'plant cell' with no reason given.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains that she can be highly confident from the wall and chloroplasts alone, and that not seeing the vacuole clearly does not weaken the conclusion, since a blurry image simply failed to show a feature that may still be there.
markingScheme.accept: Any equivalent reasoning that a missing/unclear feature is not the same as a feature being genuinely absent.
markingScheme.insufficient: Treating the unclear vacuole as evidence against the conclusion, or ignoring the vacuole issue entirely.

markingScheme.criterion: Makes a genuine real-life link: this is exactly the reasoning a food scientist or doctor uses when identifying tissue/food samples under a microscope — you don't need to see every feature to reach a confident conclusion, as long as the feature you do see is diagnostic.
markingScheme.accept: Any real-world example of identifying something from partial evidence, provided it is genuinely comparable to using one diagnostic feature.
markingScheme.insufficient: A generic 'this is useful in real life' with no actual example or comparison given.

levels.descriptor: No organelles or evidence from the photos referenced.
Mentions an organelle but does not connect it to the claim being made.
Refers to specific organelles found in the Investigation Record and links them to the claim, with a minor gap.
Clearly cites specific organelles from both real photos and uses them precisely to justify which cell is which.

criteria.source: = the Apply question's 3-point marking scheme above, one-to-one (identification + reason, confidence despite missing feature, real-life link). Do not award these 3 marks a second time here.

levels.descriptor: No attempt to reason about the new, unfamiliar cell.
States a conclusion but does not explain why.
Explains why, with one gap in the scientific logic (e.g. not addressing the missing vacuole).
Explains fully why the visible features are enough to reach a confident conclusion, correctly reasoning about the missing feature.

criteria.source: Assessed holistically across BOTH the Explain and Apply answers together — independent of, and never overlapping with, the content marks in use_of_evidence and reasoning above.

levels.descriptor: Unclear or missing sentences; no scientific terms.
Understandable but with unclear phrasing or missing key terms.
Clear, well-formed sentences using correct scientific vocabulary (organelle names used accurately).

markingInstructions: Mark ONLY the two constructed responses (Explain, Apply). Award marks point-by-point using each question's markingScheme: each point is worth the marks stated, is independent unless it names a dependsOn point (in which case only award it if that earlier point was also awarded), and each point's 'accept'/'insufficient' tell you exactly what does and doesn't count. use_of_evidence's 3 marks ARE the Explain markingScheme's 3 points, and reasoning's 3 marks ARE the Apply markingScheme's 3 points — the rubric levels restate the same points as bands; award each set of 3 marks ONCE, not twice. communication is a separate, holistic 2 marks across both answers' clarity and vocabulary, never overlapping with the content marks. Copy auto_marked_score into knowledge_accuracy (6 marks = full). Use the student's actual logged identifications and sorting decisions (the stage/organelle/result columns in simulation_results.trials) to verify any organelle the student claims to have found on a given photo — do not take their prose summary on trust if it does not match their own logged data. Accept valid alternative wording (e.g. 'permanent vacuole' for 'large vacuole', 'cell surface membrane' for 'cell membrane') per each point's 'accept' field, and do not penalise spelling unless meaning is unclear. Total is out of 14 (6 auto + 3 + 3 + 2); report total, percentage, one strength, one correction, one next step, under 80 words.
